title: India Women Knocked Out of T20 World Cup After Heartbreaking Two-Run Loss to Australia
excerpt: Australia's record-breaking 172-run chase at Lord's ends India's campaign as the defending 50-over champions fail to reach the semi-finals of the T20 showpiece.
body:
• Australia beat India by two runs (172 to 170) at Lord's to eliminate India from the Women's T20 World Cup semi-final race
  • Ellyse Perry (56) and Ash Gardner (53) powered Australia to 172 — a T20 World Cup record chase at the venue
  • India had beaten Bangladesh earlier but needed to beat Australia to progress; their campaign ends in the group stage
  • England and Australia advanced to the semi-finals, with Australia reaching their eighth final in ten editions

So Close at Lord's

India's Women's T20 World Cup campaign ended in the cruelest fashion at Lord's — two runs short of what they needed against the tournament's most dominant force. Australia posted 172-8, and India, despite a valiant effort, could manage only 170, falling agonizingly short in a match that determined semi-final qualification.

The result sent Australia through alongside hosts England from Group A, while India's defending 50-over World Cup champions were left to reflect on what might have been.

Australia's Firepower Proves Decisive

Ellyse Perry anchored the Australian innings with a typically composed 56 off 38 balls, striking eight boundaries. But it was Ash Gardner who changed the game's trajectory, smashing 53 off just 29 deliveries with three sixes, accelerating Australia to a total that proved just enough.

India's bowlers fought hard. Deepti Sharma, who was one wicket away from becoming the leading wicket-taker in women's internationals, returned respectable figures. Renuka Thakur and Sree Charani also made inroads, but Australia's depth and power hitting proved too much at the death.

India's Chase Falls Just Short

In reply, India matched Australia's aggression for much of the chase. The batting order showed intent from the start, keeping up with the required rate through the middle overs. But the loss of key wickets at crucial moments — particularly in the final five overs — left the tail with too much to do.

The two-run margin was the smallest defeat India suffered in the tournament, underscoring how thin the line is between progress and elimination at a World Cup.

What Went Wrong

India entered the tournament with mixed form — winning just 3 of 8 T20Is in 2026 before the World Cup, including a series loss to South Africa. Captain Harmanpreet Kaur's side beat Bangladesh in their group match but the loss to Australia proved fatal to their net run rate position.

The silver lining: India's women secured their Olympic berth for the LA 2028 Games earlier this year, ensuring this is not the last big stage for this generation of players. The Women's T20 World Cup final features England against Australia, with the hosts looking to exploit home advantage against a side chasing their eighth title in ten editions.
